title: HTTP Errors at the Load Balancer

scenes.say: Ever seen a five oh two or five oh three error? What do they actually tell you about your app?

scenes.sub: Bad Gateway: backend refused or sent junk
scenes.say: A five oh two means the backend refused the connection or sent something the load balancer couldn't read.

rows.b: No healthy servers in the pool

scenes.say: A five oh three means there are no healthy servers left. Five oh four means the backend was too slow to respond.
Not all errors come from the load balancer. Four oh one means authentication required. Four oh three is forbidden. Four oh four means the path doesn't exist.

scenes.question: What could cause a 503 after deploy?
scenes.right: The health check path might be missing or wrong
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: if you see a five oh three after a deploy, check if the health check path still exists. That's a common cause.
